Strongest::: Fatih Ömer İlday hoca is truly an exceptional teacher. So far he is the best instructor I met in Bilkent. He makes sure that nobody falls behind and everybody receives the same knowledge despite the fact that there were people in our class who would complete his/her MS after this semester and there were people who didn't even take any other advanced course other than calculus and general physics. In the class, we rarely faced this distinction cause he presented the contents in such a way that everybody understood. Sometimes I became inattentive in the class and I just nodded when he asked whether I understood cause it feels so bad to answer no when he is doing perfect and it is completely my fault. 
Weakest::: Once, just for once, he missed the class and we didn't receive any email. Anyway, after a week he clarified that he actually sent an email but to the wrong recipient. Sometimes in the class, he talked about statistical physics or more advanced physics (tried to make a connection to that subject with the topic we were dealing with then) but that was only suitable for a small number of people. A large number of us who have never taken that course didn't understand anything. Also, at the end of the semester, he taught us some of his research work as requested by some of us but this is so advanced from the material we covered, we are struggling to understand it. And he is also keeping the final exam as a mystery. At the beginning of the semester, he announced that the final would be non-traditional. So we will work it as a take-home assignment. And though we only have a week of class left, we didn't receive any notification about the question format of the final.

It is a bliss that this course is offered, specifically by him. You can actually see him getting excited over the things he teaches, a rare occasion considering all the other courses and their instructors.
course:
Strongest::: The recommended book of this course ("Strogatz") is so vivid and self-contained, if one studies it top to bottom, one doesn't even need to attend the lecture hours (though one should)! Everything is clearly presented in the lecture notes uploaded in the moodle. This course taught us non-linear methods that we can even use to solve some problems that we previously dealt with analytically. 

Weakest::: This course never gives you any method to solve a problem precisely and quantitatively. Almost exclusively, it teaches you how to obtain information about a system in a qualitative way. But this is only effective when there is no way to obtain that information analytically or it is hellishly difficult to treat it analytically. Also, the course teacher could present us some interactive phase-plane analysis in the screen and maybe one lecture hour about the numerical methods cause some of us didn't know about the Euler/Runge-Kutta method and we simply used pre-built Matlab script but the HW asked about writing code for Runge-Kutta method(and we never even heard about it and he didn't teach it in the class) (though it was mentioned in the book very briefly).
assistant: Xhulian Lickollari was the course assistant. He is a great guy, gave detailed feedback on the assignments, provided us the pplane8.m matlab script that we used very often in several hw and in dealing with 2D system. However, he was very strict in grading. Sometimes he just thought that whatever explanation we gave is not enough and he deducted 1 or 2 pts from every question. So even after submitting a perfect hw, you'll end up getting 95 or 96. Also, it would be really helpful if he works on his English speaking a little bit. I would give him a rating of 9 out of 10 as a TA.
Xhulian was great. The way he assidiously and attentively grades the assignments should be an example for all TAs.
